### The Cleric

```
Clerics are intermediaries between the mortal world and the distant planes of the gods. As varied as the
gods they serve, clerics strive to embody the handiwork of their deities. No ordinary priest, a cleric is
imbued with divine magic.
You must have a Wisdom modifier of +1 or higher in order to multiclass in or out of this class.
```

##### Class Features

```
Vitals
Hit Dice: 1d
Hit Points at 1st Level : 8 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 0) per cleric level after 1st
Stress Points at 1st Level: 2 + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 0)
```
```
Proficiencies
Armor: Light armor, medium armor, shields
Weapons: All simple weapons
Tools: None
Skills: Choose two from History, Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion
```
```
Equipment
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:
● (a) light, medium, or heavy armor
● (a) a simple weapon (b) a martial weapon
● (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) any simple weapon
● (a) a priest's pack or (b) an explorer's pack
● A shield and a holy symbol
```
```
Spellcasting
As a conduit for divine power, you can cast cleric spells.
```
```
Cantrips
At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the cleric spell list. You learn additional cleric
cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Cleric table.
```
```
Spell Slots
The Cleric table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your cleric spells of 1st level and higher. To
cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell
slots when you finish a long rest.
```

##### You prepare the list of druid spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the cleric spell list.

##### When you do so, choose a number of cleric spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your Cleric level

##### (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. You can change your

##### list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest.

##### For example, if you know the 1st-level spell Animal Friendship and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot

##### available, you can cast Animal Friendship using either slot.

##### Spellcasting Ability

##### Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your cleric spells, since the power of your spells comes from your

##### devotion to your deity. You use your Widom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition,

##### you use your Widom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a cleric spell you cast and when making

##### an attack roll with one.

##### Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Widom modifier

##### Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Widom modifier

##### Ritual Casting

##### You can cast a cleric spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell prepared.

#### Trait Improvement

##### When you reach 2nd level, and again at 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can

##### improve upon one of your traits listed below. You have the following choices:

##### ● Gain an additional Stress Slot

##### ● Gain a +1 bonus to a Saving Throw

##### ● Gain a +1 bonus to your Initiative

##### ● Gain proficiency in a skill, tool, or language. This option may only be chosen twice.

#### Divine Domain

##### At 1st level, you choose a domain shaped by your choice of Deity and the gifts they grant you. Your choice

##### grants you domain spells and other features when you choose it at 1st level. It also grants you additional

##### ways to use Channel Divinity when you gain that feature at 2nd level, and additional benefits at 6th, 10th,

##### 14th, and 18th level.

##### Domain

##### Light

##### Domain Spells


##### Each domain has a list of spells-its domain spells that you gain at the cleric levels noted in the domain

##### description. Once you gain a domain spell, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the

##### number of spells you can prepare each day.

##### If you have a domain spell that doesn't appear on the cleric spell list, the spell is nonetheless a cleric spell

##### for you.

#### Channel Divinity

##### At 2nd level, you gain the ability to channel divine energy directly from your deity, using that energy to fuel

##### magical effects. You start with two such effects: Turn Undead and an effect determined by your domain.

##### Some domains grant you additional effects as you advance in levels, as noted in the domain description. If

##### you use a Channel Divinity while another is still active, the previous effect immediately ends.

##### Channel Divinity: Turn Undead

##### As a Major Action, take a Stress and speak a holy prayer against the undead. Each undead that can see or

##### hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Will saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is must

##### spend its turn trying to move as far away from, and can not willingly move closer to you. It can’t take

##### reactions and can only take the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving.

#### Pious Role

##### At 3rd level, you gain benefits from the role you performed within your religion’s organization or how you

##### practiced its doctrine. Choose one of the following roles:

##### ● Archivist. You spent your days delving through knowledge and research to know your deity

##### better. You gain proficiency in Arcana and may always ritual cast any spell with the ritual tag in

##### the cleric’s spell list without preparing it. The spell can not be a level higher than your highest

##### spell slot.

##### ● Insquisitor. You were an enforcer, a weapon for your deity against enemies outside and even

##### inside the organization. You gain proficiency with martial weapons and once per turn, you may

##### add your Wisdom modifier to the damage roll of a weapon or spell attack.

##### ● Preacher. You have comitted the rites to memory and can speak for hours to spread your deity’s

##### wisdom. You gain proficiency in Performance and may use your Wisdom modifier as the basis of

##### your Fortitude saving throws.

#### Ability Improvement

##### When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase two ability

##### modifiers of your choice by 1. Alternatively, you can increase only one ability modifier of your choice by 1

##### and gain a Feat. As normal, you can't increase an ability modifier above +5 using this feature.


## Destroy Undead

## Starting at 5th level, when an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, the creature

## is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below a certain threshold, as shown in the Cleric table

## above.

## Divine Intervention

## Beginning at 9th level, you can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great. As a

## Major Action, expend up to all of your Heroic Inspiration and describe the form of assistance you require.

## The DM chooses the nature of the intervention, though the more Heroic Inspiration you use, the greater

## the effect should be.

## After using this feature, you can’t use it again until 7 days have passed. At 20th level, your call for

## intervention no longer requires Heroic Inspiration.

# Light

## Gods of light – including Helm, Lathander, Pholtus, Branchala, the Silver Flame, Belenus, Apollo, and

## Re-Horakhty – promote the ideals of rebirth and renewal, truth, vigilance, and beauty, often using the

## symbol of the sun. Some of these gods are portrayed as the sun itself or as a charioteer who guides the

## sun across the sky. Others are tireless sentinels whose eyes pierce every shadow and see through every

## deception. Some are deities of beauty and artistry, who teach that art is a vehicle for the soul's

## improvement. Clerics of a god of light are enlightened souls infused with radiance and the power of their

## gods' discerning vision, charged with chasing away lies and burning away darkness.

## Warding Flare

##### Also at 1st level, you can interpose divine light between an ally and an attacking enemy. When a creature

##### that you can see within 30 ft. of you attacks another creature, you can take a Stress as a reaction to impose

##### disadvantage on the attack roll. You must do this before knowing if the attack hits or misses. An attacker

##### that can’t be blinded or does not need to see is immune to this feature.

## Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn

##### Starting at 2nd level, you can harness sunlight to smite your foes. As a Major Action, expend a Heroic

##### Inspiration and present your holy symbol, dispelling any magic darkness within 30 ft. of you. Additionally,

##### each creature of your choice within 30 ft. of you that can see you must make a Fortitude saving throw. A

##### creature takes radiant damage equal to 2d10 + your cleric level on a failed save, and half as much on a

##### success.

##### The amount of damage dice increases when you reach 5th (3d10), 9th (4d10), 13th (5d10), and 17th

##### (6d10).

## Improved Flare

##### Starting at 6th level, when you use your Warding Flare feature, the target has disadvantage on all attack

##### rolls until the end of its turn.

## Potent Spellcasting

##### Starting at 10th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

## Blinding Radiance

##### Starting at 14th level, when you use your Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn feature, creatures that

##### fail your saving throw are also Blinded until the end of your next turn.


###### Corona of Light

```
Starting at 17th level, you can use your Major Action action to activate an aura of sunlight that lasts for 1
minute or until you dismiss it using another Major Action. You emit bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim
light 30 feet beyond that. Your enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against any
spell that deals fire or radiant damage.
```

```
close – within 30 feet – at least once. Alternatively, the spell can locate the nearest
object of a particular kind, such as a certain kind of apparel, jewelry, furniture, tool,
or weapon.
```
```
This spell can’t locate an object if any thickness of lead, even a thin sheet, blocks a
direct path between you and the object.
```
Prayer of
Healing

```
10 Minutes Instantaneous 30 ft. V Up to six creatures of your choice that you can see within range each regain 2d8 +
your spellcasting ability modifier hit points or recover 2 Stress Slots. This spell has
no effect on undead or constructs.
```
```
At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher,
the healing and stress recovery increase by 1d8 and 1 slot, respectively, for each
slot level above 2nd.
```
Silence 1 Major Action 10 Minutes
(Concentration)

```
120 ft. VS Create a 20 ft. sphere of complete silence centered around a point or object you
can see within range. If the object is being held or worn by a creature, they may
make a Reflex saving throw to instead center the spell on the space they occupy.
Creatures and objects inside the sphere is immune to thunder damage and
deafened. Casting a spell that includes a verbal component is impossible while
inside the sphere.
```
Spiritual
Weapon

```
1 Major Action 1 Minute 60 ft. VS You create a floating, spectral weapon within range that lasts for the duration or
until you cast this spell again.
```
```
When you cast the spell, you can make a melee spell attack against a creature
within 5 feet of the weapon. On a hit, the target takes force damage equal to 1d8 +
your spellcasting ability modifier.
```
```
As a minor action on subsequent turns, you can move the weapon up to 20 feet
and repeat the attack against a creature within 5 feet of it.
```

```
At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher,
the damage increases by 1d8 for every two slot levels above the 2nd.
```

rest

```
Touch VSM (a pair
of platinum
rings worth
at least 50
gp each,
which you
and target
must wear
for the
duration)
```
```
This spell wards a willing creature you touch and creates a mystic connection
between you and the target until the spell ends.
```
```
While the target is within 60 feet of you, it gains a +1 bonus to AC and saving
throws, and it has resistance to all damage. Also, each time it takes damage, you
take the same amount of damage.
```
```
The spell ends if you drop to 0 hit points or if you and the target become separated
by more than 60 feet. It also ends if the spell is cast again on either of the
connected creatures. You can also dismiss the spell as an action.
```
